editions.intro: Nvidia’s board weighing the future of chief executive Jensen Huang leads the NYT and the BBC this morning. The Washington Post leads with the Democratic Senate win in Mississippi, and readers in the US are also clicking on Pete Hegseth being scolded at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
editions.cover: Nvidia leads the morning: the New York Times and both BBC homepages open with its board weighing the future of chief executive Jensen Huang, after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and a relationship with an executive who reports to him. The Washington Post leads with Democrat Scott Colom’s Senate win in Mississippi, which also tops the Guardian’s most-viewed list, while Pete Hegseth being scolded at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is No. 1 on the Post’s most-read list. The Guardian’s UK edition still leads with the David Walliams fallout, and the Times of Israel’s newest item is Hezbollah’s leader on the elections. Away from the news, Pochettino is set to take over Manchester United, Dua Lipa will headline Coachella, and Israeli outlets review the new season of “HaTabach.”

leading.headline: Nvidia’s Board Is Meeting to Discuss Jensen Huang’s Future
leading.text: Nvidia’s board is meeting about its chief executive after reports of his affair with a woman US intelligence calls a Chinese spy and of a relationship with an executive who reports to him; the NYT says the stock fell more than 8 percent after hours.
leading.ranks: Leads: NYT, BBC (UK and international), Guardian (international), Sky News. Most read No. 1: NYT. On the front: WaPo, The Times (X).

leading.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Senate race in Mississippi
leading.text: Colom beat Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith by a very thin margin, with the race called eight days after election day; the Post says he will be the state’s first Black senator since the end of Reconstruction.
leading.ranks: Leads: WaPo. Top 5: BBC (international), Guardian (international), NYT. Most read: Guardian No. 1 and No. 3, WaPo No. 2. Also on Sky News.

leading.headline: Hegseth and his entourage scolded by military sentinel at Tomb of the Unknowns
leading.text: A guard at Arlington National Cemetery told the defense secretary, his wife and aides to keep silent and show respect after they were seen laughing and talking on Veterans Day; separately, the NYT says 11 Democrats missed the vote that shelved his impeachment and now face criticism.
leading.ranks: Top 3: WaPo. Most read: WaPo No. 1, NYT trending No. 4 (No. 5 for the missed vote), Guardian No. 4. Also: BBC top-stories video, The Times (X).

leading.text: The fallout from the allegations against the British comedian goes on, and the Guardian reports ministers warning the TV industry to tackle abuse or face a crackdown; Walliams denies the allegations.
leading.ranks: Leads: Guardian (UK). Top 3: BBC (UK). Most read No. 1: BBC. Also on BBC international and ynet entertainment.

editions.cover: The big newsrooms split on what matters most today. The New York Times leads with the woman at the center of the Nvidia spy scandal, which is also No. 1 on the Times and Washington Post most-read lists. The Post leads with House Republicans blocking the Hegseth impeachment. In Britain, The Guardian and The Times lead with the allegations against David Walliams, which he denies, and the BBC's top stories include the arrest of a US Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia. The Times of Israel leads with Netanyahu's Knesset speech. Away from the news pages, M John Harrison became the first science fiction author to win the Booker Prize, Stacy Keach died at 85, and Paul McCartney became a billionaire.
